LESSON: COMMUNICATION IN EASTERN AFRICA

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Resources and Economic Activities in Eastern Africa
Topic 3.5: Communication in Eastern Africa
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Communication in Eastern Africa, part of Resources and Economic Activities in Eastern Africa in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How does communication network influence the development of our country?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Communication in Eastern Africa together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: A learner develops speaking, writing and teamwork skills as they role play scenarios

that depict the different modes of communication in Eastern Africa.

• Learning to learn: A learner acquires the skill of carrying out research or investigations as they discuss the challenges

and solutions to challenges facing communication networks in Eastern Africa.

Values:
• Peace: Learners are open minded as they brainstorm, in pairs, and state challenges facing communication networks in

Eastern Africa.

• Respect: Learners take turns in discussing challenges facing communication networks in Eastern Africa.

• Unity: Learners role play the different modes of communication networks in Eastern Africa.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Social cohesion: Learners role play scenarios that depict the different modes of communication in Eastern Africa.

• Safety and Security: A learner researches on challenges facing communication networks in Eastern Africa

Link to other Learning Areas:

• Learners apply Pre-technical studies knowledge as they discuss in groups solutions to challenges facing

communication networks in Eastern Africa.

46

• Learners use English/Kiswahili/Kenya sign language as they state solutions facing communication networks in Eastern

Africa.

Suggested Learning Resources:

• Maps, tactile maps of Eastern Africa, mobile phone, Radio, Magazine or newspaper, e-mail, digital devices with assistive

technology, approved appropriate print or braille Social studies textbooks and other relevant materials
